text.p: Mining service firms Eltin Ltd and Ausdrill Ltd said on Tuesday they had been awarded a contract worth an estimated A$135 million at the Tarkwa gold project in Ghana, West Africa.
The companies said they had been awarded an initial five year contract for surface mining of the Akontansi and Pepe open pits at Tarkwa, 250 kilometres west of Accra.
The project is owned by Gold Fields Ghana Ltd, a 70 percent-owned unit of Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd.
Gold Fields is South Africa's third largest gold producer and has previously operated underground mines.

The companies said the 50-50 contract involved the movement of 78 million tonnes of material, commencing at nine million tonnes per year and increasing to 20 million tonnes per year after the second year of operations.
Mobilisation for the contact would commence in March 1997, with pre-development work starting in June and production mining expected to start on September 15 next year.
An estimated A$25 million of new plant and equipment would be required for the contact which would be shared equally between Eltin and Ausdrill.
